pr_title: planner: choose non-prefix column when both index key and handle have the same one
pr_body: Signed-off-by: lysu ### What problem does this PR solve? Issue Number: close #22960 Problem Summary: user can create a index contain two same column values in one index with clustered index support. for example, we have a table `t` ``` create table t( c1 varchar(100), c2 varchar(100), c3 varchar(100), primary key (c1,c2) clustered, key idx1 (c2(1)), ) ``` then for an IndexReader Query: ``` select c2 from t use index(idx1) where c = 'x'; ``` IndexQuery will have information about 2 `c2`, one from index value, and another from primary key value(CommonHandle) if there are no prefix column, operator above IndexReader can choose any of those two columns but if there is a prefix column like this table schema, planner need make all operators above is use non-prefix column ### What is changed and how it works? What's Changed: make ColumnIndex to prefer choose full column ### Related changes - n/a ### Check List Tests - Unit test - Side effects - n/a ### Release note - n/a --- This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/pingcap/tidb/22980)

issue_context.title: prefix column in secondary index in clustered index table maybe return wrong result
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```
set @@tidb_enable_clustered_index=1;
create table t(c1 varchar(100), c2 varchar(100), c3 varchar(100), primary key (c1,c2), key idx1 (c2(1)));
insert into t select 'a', 'cd', 'ef';
select c2 from t use index(idx1);
select count(1) from t use index(idx1) where c2 = 'cd';
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

```
cd
1
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```
c
0
```
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

master
<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
